attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The only unquarantined escape is to construct a nonprojection carrier with N^{o(1)} target query length, sub-N^{1+epsilon} interface size, and a valid N^{1+epsilon} nonuniform lower bound.
steps: Assume SAT has nonuniform circuits of size O(m^c) for every queried formula length m.
Model the carrier algorithm as an oracle circuit A_N with explicit ordinary gates and explicit SAT-query gates; adaptivity is absorbed into the circuit DAG.
Replace each SAT-query gate of length at most N^{beta+o(1)} by the corresponding SAT circuit of size N^{beta c+o(1)}.
The resulting L_N circuit has size at most N^{a+o(1)}+N^{q+beta c+o(1)}.
Contrapose against SIZE(L_N)>N^{1+epsilon}: only exponents c satisfying q+beta c<1+epsilon and a<1+epsilon are ruled out.
Therefore a positive polynomial query-length exponent beta is a quantitative threshold-collapse falsifier for deriving NP not subset P/poly from one fixed barely-superlinear source lower bound.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a bridge cap and a route failure criterion, not a lower bound for any explicit carrier and not P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: black-box substitution cap

assumptions: epsilon>0 is fixed independently of c.
The source lower bound is for the same nonuniform circuit model used after substitution.
SAT in SIZE(m^c) means a circuit family of size O(m^c) for every relevant target length m.
Adaptive queries are represented as oracle gates in A_N, so gate-by-gate substitution is legitimate.
definitions: source object: a length-indexed Boolean carrier L_N subset {0,1}^N with lower bound against nonuniform Boolean circuits of size N^{1+epsilon} on the stated valid lengths.
target object: SAT_m with target consequence SAT notin SIZE(m^c); exclusion for every fixed c would imply NP not subset P/poly by standard NP-completeness transfer.
controlled interface: a nonuniform SAT-oracle circuit A_N deciding L_N with ordinary size N^{a+o(1)}, at most N^{q+o(1)} oracle gates, and queried formula length at most N^{beta+o(1)}.

target-preserving condition: all advice and preprocessing are counted in A_N, only SAT circuits are substituted for oracle gates, valid source lengths map to bounded target lengths, and no hidden nonuniform witness search is used.

equations.label: substitution_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source oracle circuit explicitly counts advice, preprocessing, and every SAT oracle gate before substitution.

equations.label: contrapositive_window
equations.latex: SIZE(L_N)>N^{1+\epsilon} \Rightarrow SAT \notin SIZE(m^c) \text{ for } c<\frac{1+\epsilon-q}{\beta}, \ a<1+\epsilon, \ \beta>0
equations.valid_when: Applies after the reduction preserves target lengths and the lower bound holds on matching valid source lengths.

equations.label: all_exponent_obstruction
equations.latex: \forall c\;[SAT\notin SIZE(m^c)] \text{ from fixed } \epsilon \text{ requires } \beta=0 \text{ and } \max\{a,q\}<1+\epsilon
equations.valid_when: Requires fixed epsilon and black-box substitution as the only target-preserving complexity-class transfer mechanism.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If beta>0, or q>=1+epsilon, or a>=1+epsilon, the intended all-exponent bridge is invalid even before invoking natural proofs, relativization, or algebrization.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route audit lemma: it certifies exactly when a black-box SAT-oracle carrier can magnify a barely-superlinear source lower bound and when threshold collapse is a falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let L_N be an N-bit carrier with nonuniform lower bound SIZE(L_N)>N^{1+epsilon} on infinitely many valid lengths. If L has an oracle-circuit reduction to SAT using N^{a+o(1)} non-oracle size, N^{q+o(1)} SAT queries, and maximum query length N^{beta+o(1)}, then the bridge excludes only SAT circuits of exponent c with a<1+epsilon and q+beta c<1+epsilon. Thus any fixed beta>0 gives a finite exponent window, not NP not subset P/poly.

assumptions: The target lower bound sought is all fixed polynomial exponents for SAT.
The source lower bound remains barely superlinear in the ambient N-bit input length.
definitions: source model: nonuniform Boolean circuits on N-bit carrier inputs.
escape condition: beta=0 with maximum SAT query length N^{o(1)} and total oracle-gate count N^{q+o(1)} for q<1+epsilon.
barrier status: the substitution lemma is relativizing and black-box; success must enter through a nonprojection carrier lower bound or a nonblack-box use of SAT structure.
quarantine condition: if the carrier is merely padding or projection of an m-bit SAT instance, the previous projection-sandwich demagnification applies.

equations.label: subpoly_query_transfer
equations.latex: SAT\in SIZE(m^c),\ m\le N^{o(1)} \Rightarrow SIZE(L_N)\le N^{\max\{a,q\}+o(1)} \text{ for each fixed } c
equations.valid_when: Valid when c is fixed before N tends to infinity and query lengths are genuinely subpolynomial.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any proof that the subpolynomial-query carrier lower bound is equivalent to an N^{omega(1)} lower bound for the embedded target object.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Identifies the only remaining black-box parameter regime after cycles 1-6.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A black-box route can still formally evade the exponent cap only by using SAT queries of length N^{o(1)} and total oracle-interface size below N^{1+epsilon}. This escape does not prove a separation; it moves the burden to proving an N^{1+epsilon} lower bound for a carrier whose useful SAT information is subpolynomial in the input length.

control_decision.pivot_test: Search for a carrier whose SAT information has query length N^{o(1)} and interface size below N^{1+epsilon}, then test whether its lower bound demagnifies to a strong target lower bound.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if the next carrier satisfies beta=0, max{a,q}<1+epsilon, and avoids the projection-sandwich equivalence.
control_decision.reason: All polynomial-query black-box bridges are now quantitatively capped and cannot yield NP not subset P/poly from one fixed N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound.

dependency_updates.description: Replaced the slogan by a black-box oracle-substitution inequality with parameters a,q,beta,epsilon,c.
Source is nonuniform SIZE lower bound for N-bit carrier L_N on valid lengths; no uniform algorithmic lower bound is being smuggled in.
The bridge yields SAT notin SIZE(m^c) only inside the computed exponent window unless beta=0.
The cap is relativizing and black-box. Natural-proofs and algebrization barriers are not the immediate obstruction; the formal obstruction is quantitative nonuniform substitution leakage.

falsifiers: falsifier: beta>0 leaves only the finite window c<(1+epsilon-q)/beta, so all-exponent NP/poly separation cannot follow.
falsifier: q>=1+epsilon means the oracle interface alone already exceeds the source lower-bound threshold.
falsifier: a>=1+epsilon means preprocessing or advice leakage consumes the entire barely-superlinear margin.
falsifier: projection or padding carriers with subpolynomial query length demagnify the source lower bound into a strong target lower bound, as in the earlier projection-sandwich quarantine.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 7 generalizes the MCSP and padding failures to an oracle-interface theorem. A barely-superlinear carrier lower bound transfers through a black-box SAT interface as max{a,q+beta c}; hence positive target-query length exponent beta is the decisive threshold-collapse falsifier. The remaining valid route must either use subpolynomial target queries with a genuinely nonprojection carrier or abandon black-box substitution.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Test a succinct local-consistency or proof-complexity carrier with N^{o(1)} SAT queries: compute a,q,beta, then run the projection-demagnification falsifier before claiming any magnification.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No local NP-checkable or E-time certificate is supplied for the statement that the chosen prefix remains outside every size-s circuit truth table.
steps: Set N=2^n and list all size-s circuits on n inputs; there are 2^{O(s log s)} descriptions.
Evaluate each listed circuit on all N inputs and mark its N-bit truth table.
Choose the lexicographically first unmarked N-bit string y_n and define L_s(x)=y_n[x].
By construction, the n-bit slice of L_s is not computed by any size-s circuit.
The direct bit algorithm recomputes the marked set or an equivalent avoidance certificate, costing 2^n 2^{O(s log s)} poly(n,s).
Thus E preservation forces s log s=O(n), while polynomial lower-bound thresholds s=n^k for k>1 move the language outside E and far outside NP.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is valid route-level progress only. It quarantines a counting selector bridge; it does not prove P != NP, and its relativizing exhaustive step cannot by itself cross known oracle barriers.

assumptions: Circuits are fan-in two Boolean circuits over a fixed finite basis.
The number of size-s circuits on n inputs is at most 2^{O(s log s)} after standard encoding.
To select the lexicographically first missing truth table, the route has no nonenumerative certificate of absence from all size-s circuit truth tables.
Target E means DTIME(2^{O(n)}) for n-bit inputs; target NP requires polynomial-time verifiable witnesses.
definitions: source object: lexicographic circuit-avoidance selector over all Boolean circuits of size at most s(n) for n-bit functions.
target object: a uniform language L_s whose n-bit truth table avoids SIZE(s(n)), with intended target class NP or E and lower-bound threshold s(n)=n^k.
controlled interface: enumeration of circuit descriptions plus target-preserving computation of selected truth-table bits from input x without advice.
target-preserving condition: the bit L_s(x) must be computable inside the named target class while preserving the same input length n and size threshold s(n).
barrier posture: the selector is non-large, so the usual natural-proof largeness premise is absent, but the construction is relativizing and quantitatively too slow for the intended target.

equations.label: circuit_count
equations.valid_when: Valid when circuits use a fixed finite basis and standard descriptions with O(s log s) bits.

equations.label: selector_time
equations.valid_when: Applies when the selector constructs or queries the avoided table by exhaustive circuit enumeration.

equations.label: E_threshold
equations.valid_when: Requires comparing the exhaustive selector running time with the E time bound on n-bit inputs.

equations.label: polynomial_size_collapse
equations.valid_when: Valid when k is fixed above one and the enumeration term dominates the truth-table length.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any route claiming NP or E membership for the selected hard language at s(n)=n^2 without replacing exhaustive avoidance by a target-preserving local certificate.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quantitative threshold-collapse certificate for counting/diagonalization routes.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Lexicographic avoidance of size-s circuits gives a uniform hard truth table only at the enumeration threshold. For n-bit functions, N=2^n, the selector is target-preserving for E only when s(n)log s(n)=O(n); at s(n)=n^k with k>1 it lands in DTIME(2^{Theta(n^k log n)}) and gives no valid NP or E lower-bound bridge.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the next proposal still uses global enumeration or advice to certify hard truth tables.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if a nonrelativizing, no-advice, locally checkable selector computes y_n[x] in NP or E while preserving s(n)=n^k for some k>1.
control_decision.reason: The route has a precise quantitative collapse: the only proved target-preserving regime gives at most near-linear circuit lower bounds for E, while the desired polynomial thresholds leave the target class.

dependency_updates.description: Added the selector threshold s log s=O(n) as the exact boundary where exhaustive circuit avoidance remains inside E.
Raw circuit-counting avoidance relativizes to oracle circuits, so it is not a nonrelativizing proof object.
The construction avoids largeness by selecting one hard table, hence natural proofs do not directly apply; the valid blocker is constructivity collapse.
Any repair using advice must account for advice large enough to encode the avoided table or enumeration witness.

falsifiers: falsifier: s(n)=n^2 yields selector time 2^{Theta(n^2 log n)}, invalidating any claimed E-preserving transfer by raw counting.
falsifier: advice of length 2^{O(s log s)} can encode the relevant avoidance information, so advice-bearing targets suffer nonuniform leakage.
falsifier: the same circuit enumeration works relative to an oracle, so a fully relativizing version cannot imply an unrelativized P != NP separation.
falsifier: calling the selected table non-natural is insufficient; the obstruction here is explicitness and target-time collapse.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 7 turns counting-diagonalization optimism into a concrete threshold lemma: exhaustive lexicographic avoidance yields hard slices, but preserves E only for s log s=O(n). Polynomial thresholds such as n^2 require 2^{Theta(n^2 log n)} time, so the bridge is invalid for NP and for E at the desired lower-bound scale. This is valid barrier-aware route progress, not evidence for P != NP.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Test whether an MCSP-gap certificate can replace global circuit enumeration: source GapMCSP_{s,2s}, target NP language, threshold s=n^k, with audits for natural-proof largeness and advice leakage.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No construction is known for a sound verifier with O(m)-bit certificates and kappa-gap existence that is not already smuggling in the desired lower bound.
steps: Replace the nonuniform hard truth-table carrier by a uniform search space of compact pairs (u,pi).
Use V-soundness so that every accepted pair defines a genuinely high-MCSP function f_u, rather than an advised candidate.
For each target length n, scan source lengths m in [ceil(n/kappa),n] and all O(m)-bit pairs until an accepted pair is found.
Define L on n-bit inputs by applying the selected decoder to the first m bits and ignoring the padding bits.
The search and evaluation cost is 2^{O(n)}, so L is in E.
If L_n had circuits of size 2^{delta n}, fixing the ignored bits would give circuits for f_u of size 2^{delta n}+O(n).
Since m>=n/kappa and delta<epsilon/kappa, this contradicts V-soundness for all large n.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The bridge is valid conditional route progress only. It reduces the route to building a sparse non-natural uniform certificate source; it does not prove P != NP or even unconditionally produce the E lower bound.

branch_outputs.branch_title: MCSP / Meta-Complexity Carrier Transfer, Cycle 7: Searchable Certificate Repair

assumptions: Constants epsilon>0, kappa>=1, c>0 are fixed independently of m and n.
Soundness is semantic: V(1^m,u,pi)=1 implies every Boolean circuit computing f_u has size greater than 2^{epsilon m}.
For every sufficiently large n, some m in [ceil(n/kappa),n] has an accepted pair (u,pi) with |u|+|pi|<=c m.
The decoder D(u,z) computes f_u(z) deterministically in 2^{O(m)} time.
definitions: source object: a searchable succinct no-side MCSP certificate system (V,D) where a code u defines f_u:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, V(1^m,u,pi) is deterministic, and acceptance soundly implies CC(f_u)>2^{epsilon m}.
target object: an all-large-length language L in E=DTIME(2^{O(n)}) satisfying CC(L_n)>2^{delta n} for each sufficiently large input length n.
controlled interface: on input length n, search m in [ceil(n/kappa),n] and all pairs (u,pi) of total length at most c m; select the first accepted pair and set L(x)=D(u,prefix_m(x)).
target-preserving condition: V and D run in 2^{O(m)}, witnesses have length O(m), accepted pairs exist in every kappa-gap interval, and no advice or nonuniform selector is used.

equations.label: search_time
equations.valid_when: Valid when code-plus-proof length is linear in m and both verifier and decoder have single-exponential running time.

equations.label: padding_transfer
equations.valid_when: Applies when L_n is defined by f_u on the first m input bits and the remaining n-m bits are fixed.

equations.label: exponent_margin
equations.valid_when: Requires a fixed positive exponent margin epsilon/kappa minus delta on sufficiently large input lengths.

equations.label: target_lower_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid after the sound accepted certificate is found in every kappa-gap interval without advice.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: if accepted pairs are only nonuniformly chosen, have superlinear total length, or occur with unbounded gaps, the E target or exponent transfer is invalid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Conditional bridge lemma proved under its source assumptions; it is a valid route-level transfer, not a proof of P != NP.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Searchable succinct high-MCSP certificates with constant gap imply an all-large-length E lower bound. Fix epsilon>0 and kappa>=1. If a deterministic certificate verifier soundly accepts only decoders for m-bit functions of circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m}, has O(m)-bit searchable certificates, and has an accepted pair in every interval [ceil(n/kappa),n], then for every delta<epsilon/kappa there is L in E with CC(L_n)>2^{delta n} for all sufficiently large n.

assumptions: The construction does not receive the accepted pair as advice.
The verifier is total and deterministic, so failed candidates can be rejected during search.
The target is specifically E, not EXP or subexponential nonuniformity.
definitions: source object: the same certificate carrier as C7.1 but with variable witness length ell(m) and verifier time T_V(m).
target object: E-uniform extraction rather than nonuniform truth-table selection.
controlled interface: exhaustive search over all candidate decoders and proofs before evaluating the selected decoder.
target-preserving condition: ell(m)+log T_V(m)+log T_D(m)=O(m) on the searched interval.

equations.label: general_search_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies when the extractor searches every candidate witness up to the declared length bound for each source length.

equations.label: threshold_collapse
equations.latex: \ell(m)=m^{1+\alpha}\Rightarrow T_L(n)\ge 2^{\Omega(n^{1+\alpha})}\text{ in the black-box search implementation}
equations.valid_when: Valid when no additional structure permits finding accepted certificates faster than exhaustive enumeration.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: any proposed certificate family with superlinear searchable mass cannot support the advertised E lower-bound transfer.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quantitative falsifier lemma for the uniform extraction dependency.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Linear searchable mass is the sharp uniformity threshold for this carrier. With witness length ell(m) and verifier time T_V(m), exhaustive source search places the extracted language in DTIME(2^{O(max_{m<=n}(ell(m)+log T_V(m)+log T_D(m)))}). Thus ell(m)=m^{1+Omega(1)} or log T_V(m)=m^{1+Omega(1)} collapses the claimed E consequence to a larger time class.

assumptions: The distinguisher can evaluate R_m on explicit truth tables in polynomial time in N.
Every function generated by the PRF family has circuit size below N^epsilon for large m.
The PRF security is against poly(N)-time distinguishers with inverse-polynomial advantage.
definitions: source object: a truth-table property R_m obtained by forgetting the proof object and accepting x when some certificate makes V accept x.
target object: usefulness against SIZE(N^epsilon) for N=2^m truth tables.
controlled interface: constructivity from the full truth table in poly(N) time and largeness under the uniform random truth table distribution.
target-preserving condition: avoid dense P-decidable properties unless the route also supplies a non-natural or PRF-breaking ingredient.

equations.label: natural_advantage
equations.valid_when: Applies when R_m is large on random truth tables and rejects every truth table computed by the small PRF circuit family.

equations.label: usefulness
equations.valid_when: Valid when the certificate soundness excludes all circuits of size N to the epsilon for the represented truth table.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: if the proposed MCSP certificate is merely a large constructive property, it is blocked by the natural-proofs formal obstruction under standard PRF assumptions.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier classifier; it quarantines natural dense source attempts but does not refute sparse proof-certificate carriers.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Dense truth-table constructivization of the source certificate is a natural-proofs obstruction. If the accepted objects induce a poly(N)-time decidable property R_m of N=2^m-bit truth tables, R_m has density at least 1/poly(N), and R_m excludes SIZE(N^epsilon), then exponentially secure PRFs in SIZE(N^epsilon) would be distinguished. Therefore a viable source certificate must be sparse, proof-object dependent, non-natural, or outside the PRF regime.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if every candidate verifier either induces a dense truth-table property, requires superlinear proof/search length, or selects decoders nonuniformly.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only upon a concrete sound verifier V with O(m)-bit searchable certificates accepted on kappa-gap lengths at MCSP threshold 2^{epsilon m}, without relying on the extracted lower bound as an assumption.
control_decision.reason: A route-specific bridge lemma is now proved and quantitatively preserves the target, but its source object is unconstructed and must avoid naturalness, advice, and superlinear search mass.

dependency_updates.description: The carrier is no longer a named hard truth table; it is a uniformly searchable compact certificate whose accepted decoder denotes a high-MCSP function.
C7.1 proves the transfer from O(m)-searchable kappa-gap certificates at threshold 2^{epsilon m} to E lower bounds with every delta<epsilon/kappa.
Explicitness is exactly ell(m)+log T_V(m)+log T_D(m)=O(m) plus no advice; superlinear searchable mass is a formal falsifier.
Dense constructive truth-table versions of the certificate route are blocked under exponential PRFs; sparse proof-object certificates remain outside this known barrier's direct scope.
Uniform exhaustive search removes advice only when witnesses are linearly bounded and verifier rejection is total and deterministic.

falsifiers: falsifier: accepted pairs exist only via advice-selected (u_m,pi_m), causing nonuniform leakage and invalidating the E target.
falsifier: |u|+|pi|=m^{1+Omega(1)} or T_V(m)=2^{m^{1+Omega(1)}}, so exhaustive extraction leaves E.
falsifier: accepted source lengths have gap kappa(n)->infty, forcing the lower-bound exponent delta to collapse to 0.
falsifier: the certificate set becomes a dense poly(N)-time decidable truth-table property, triggering the natural-proofs obstruction under exponentially secure PRFs.
falsifier: V certifies only average-case, approximate, or promise MCSP hardness without a reduction to exact worst-case circuit lower bound for f_u.
falsifier: D uses randomized choices or hidden advice, so the constructed language is not a deterministic uniform E language.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 7 repairs the circular carrier by making the source a searchable proof-like object. The valid bridge now has a sharp threshold: O(m)-bit sound certificates on kappa-gap source lengths yield E lower bounds with exponent delta<epsilon/kappa. The remaining task is not another hardness-magnification slogan but construction of a sparse, non-natural, nonuniform-free certificate source; dense constructive variants hit the natural-proofs falsifier.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Try to instantiate V as a sparse proof-complexity certificate for succinct lower-bound tautologies LB(u,2^{epsilon m}); measure proof-code length, verifier time, gap coverage, and whether the induced accepted truth-table set is non-natural rather than dense.

Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
